description:
FILED s484b (Opus, 2026-09-13) with #1117's shape (B).

#1117 made a CLEARED aggregate slot read as ABSENT by registering the empty
container `%p-glob-clear-var-slot` installs in `*p-removed-agg-slots*`.  Two
spellings meet in that helper â `undef *G` and `*A = *B`'s missing-slot half
â and both now match perl.  There is a THIRD clear path that does not:
`%p-glob-clear` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp), the `local *G` localizer, which
installs its own fresh empties inline (`(make-array 0 â¦)`, `(make-hash-table
:test 'equal)`) and registers nothing.

PROBED 5.40.3 vs PCL (scratch/s484b/probe/t5-local.pl):

    our @a = (1,2);
    { local *a;
      *a{ARRAY}          perl undef   PCL ref     <-- diverges
      push @a, 9;
      *a{ARRAY}          perl ref     PCL ref     agree
    }
    *a{ARRAY} (after)    perl ref     PCL ref     agree   (@a is (1,2) again)

NOT DONE IN s484b for two reasons, both stated rather than assumed: the s480
design and the USER's ruling scope the fix to `%p-glob-clear-var-slot`
("do not add a second registration site"), and no test row in any of the four
populations is known to ask the question inside a `local *G` scope.

FIX SHAPE (S): `%p-glob-clear` takes its empties from `%p-glob-empty-slot`
(it duplicates that knowledge today â pre-existing, rule 11) and registers
the two aggregate ones, which is then ONE line.  The bar is the full sweep
plus the `local *FH` population (`local *FH` is a common idiom: grep the
sweep and companion for it), because a slot reading ABSENT inside a local
scope is a behaviour change for every one of them.  Residue stays the #1117
one: a read does not re-vivify.

=== DONE (s484c) ===
SHIPPED 2026-09-14, commit "s484c member 4 (#1727): `local *G` registers the
empties it installs" (runtime-only; no generation bump).

%p-glob-clear spelled all three empties inline and registered nothing, so
*a{ARRAY} read PRESENT inside a `local *a` scope where perl says undef.  The
empties now come from %p-glob-empty-slot -- the ONE reading of what an emptied
slot holds -- and the two aggregates are registered, the same registration
%p-glob-clear-var-slot makes.  The SCALAR slot needs none.

MEASURED: 9 probe rows identical to perl 5.40.3 (slot absent inside the scope
for both sigils, present again after a write, the outer container back on exit,
the assigning spelling `local *t = \@src` present throughout, the scalar slot
always a ref, the `local *FH` + `open FH` idiom still reading its line).  THE
POPULATION: the 9 perl-tests/ files using `local *` are byte-identical per file
to a base extraction, and the 33 companion t/ files that use it were run
--jobs 1 with their five snapshot-differing files A/B'd on the base and
identical there.  Guard Pl/t/glob-undef-01.t row 11, inverse-verified.  ir-spec
Â§7.2 and not-supported.md both say `local` now.  Residue: #1117's own (a read
does not re-vivify), plus #1753 and #1754 filed from the same probes.
subject: `local *G` installs fresh empties WITHOUT registering them, so `*G{ARRAY}` reads present inside the scope where perl says undef (the third clear path, #1117's family)
